title: Group Files by Identical Content
statement:
A file listing is given as an array of strings dirs. Each string describes one folder: the folder path, then one or more files, all separated by single spaces. Each file is written as name(content). For example "web/src app.js(xyz) util.js(abc)" means the folder web/src holds app.js with content xyz and util.js with content abc.

Find every set of files whose contents are exactly equal. Return them as groups of full paths, written folder/name. Only include groups with at least two files.

Any order is accepted, both for the groups and for the paths inside a group.

examples.in: dirs = ["web/src app.js(xyz) util.js(abc)", "web/lib vendor.js(xyz)", "docs readme.md(abc) notes.md(qq)"]
examples.why: Two contents appear twice. notes.md has unique content, so it is left out.
No two files share content, so there are no groups.
Equal names do not matter; three different files share the content "hi".

constraints: Folder paths, names and contents use letters, digits, '.' and '/' (paths only); no spaces or parentheses inside them
Folder paths are distinct; file names are distinct within a folder
hints: The key question for each file is "which other files have the same content?". What structure answers that in one pass?
Use the content itself as a hash map key, and collect full paths in a list per key.

Parse each string: the first token is the folder; for every other token split at the first '(' to get the name and the content (dropping the final ')'). At the end keep only lists with two or more paths.

explain.intuition:
Grouping things that are equal is the job of a hash map. Here the key is the file content and the value is the list of full paths that have it. After one pass over every file, each list is one group of duplicates, and you only keep the lists with more than one path.

The rest is parsing. Split a line on spaces: the first piece is the folder, every other piece is name(content). Cut at the ( and drop the trailing ). This is the same idea as finding duplicate uploads by hashing their bytes.
steps: Create a map from content to a list of paths.
For each line, split on spaces. Take the first piece as folder.
For every other piece, find the index of (. The name is before it, the content is between it and the last character.
Append folder + "/" + name to the list for that content.
Return every list that has at least two paths.
pitfalls: Returning groups of size one. Unique files are not duplicates.
Grouping by file name instead of content. Same name in different folders means nothing here.
Comparing every pair of files directly. That is quadratic in the number of files, while the map is linear in the input size.

complexity.time: O(L), where L is the total input length

solutions.title: Compare every pair of files
solutions.idea: List every file with its content, then link each file to every earlier file with equal content.
solutions.time: O(F² · c) for F files of content length c

solutions.title: Hash map from content to paths
solutions.idea: Parse every file once and append its full path to the list for its content. Keep lists with two or more paths.

followups: The files are real and some are gigabytes. How would you avoid reading every byte of every file? (Think size first, then a hash of a small chunk, then a full hash, then a byte compare.)
Two different contents can have the same hash. How do you make sure a reported group is really identical?
